title: `sum` of integers: widened below 32 bits, wraps at 32 and 64; 0 for no values
description: `sum` of `Int8`, `Int16`, `UInt8` and `UInt16` returns `Int64`; `Int32` and `Int64` keep their type and wrap, ungrouped and grouped (`Int32` 2³¹-1 + 1 is -2³¹).
The sum of no values, or of NULLs only, is 0, also per group: Substrait's `sum0`. `product` of no values is 1.

Both engines wrap, by different code: in memory `wrapping_sum_arr` calls `wrapping_add`; the streaming `NumSumReducer` adds with `+=`, which wraps because Polars's release builds leave overflow checks off.
The docs are silent on `Int32` and `Int64` sums wrapping: a docs gap.
No upstream test pins the wrap; it may change between versions.
reference: `sum` of integers returns the input type, with `overflow: ERROR` (an inferred precondition checked on the data, #316, #437), and NULL for no values (`functions_arithmetic.yaml`: "The sum of zero elements yields null").

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

notes: Streaming gives what in memory gives on every probe and observation cited here.
The observations' frames hold a few rows, which streaming runs as one-row morsels; the probes' 6000-row columns cover morsels of many rows.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each probe one row at a time and on a 6000-row column with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')`, and each observation twice: its `df(...)` frame's `select`, `with_columns`, `filter`, `sort`, `unique`, `join` and `group_by` go through the streaming engine the second time (`StreamingFrame`); the `s-` observations collect a lazy query on each engine themselves. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

evidence.note: SumCast: u8, u16, i8, i16 sum as i64; u32, u64, i32, i64 keep their type
streaming new_sum_reduction: NumSumReducer per physical type; null_on_empty uses VecMaskGroupedReduction
streaming: init zero; reduce_one, reduce_ca and combine use `+=`, which wraps in release builds
release profile: lto and debug only, overflow-checks stay off

provenance.notes: Added to the description: the in-memory and streaming kernels and why both wrap.

evidence.note: states Int8/UInt8/Int16/UInt16 → Int64 and 0 for no non-null values; silent on Int32/Int64 wrapping
`test_list_sum_and_dtypes`: sum dtypes Int8/Int16/UInt8/UInt16 → Int64, Int32 → Int32, Int64 → Int64 (eager)
`test_count_guarded_sum`, in-memory and streaming: when(count > 0).then(sum) becomes sum(null_on_empty=true), same result. No upstream test of integer overflow wrapping
streaming grouped sums over every integer dtype match the eager total
